definition_en: totally and in every way; to the fullest degree
core_image: 一杯水被一口气喝光，一滴不剩
scene: 考试结束铃响了，小明忽然发现有一整页题没做，心一下子凉透了。I had forgotten that page, so my answers were completely wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 completely 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：程度达到顶点、一点不剩）；句意是我整页没做，答案全错了。

derivatives.zh: 由 complete 加副词后缀构成，义为「完整的；完成的」
义为「完成；使完整」

senses.title: To the greatest degree possible
senses.definition: totally, in every way, with nothing left out
senses.definitionCN: 在所有方面都如此，毫无保留
senses.example: The bottle was completely empty after the football match.
senses.exampleCN: 踢完足球赛后瓶子全空了。
senses.why: The core image is finishing something down to the last drop, so the adverb pushes the meaning all the way to the end.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把事情做到最后一滴也不剩，所以这个副词把程度推到顶点。

senses.title: In every part; wholly
senses.definition: in every part or detail; wholly so
senses.definitionCN: 在每个部分或细节上都如此
senses.example: My answer was completely different from hers.
senses.exampleCN: 我的答案和她的完全不同。
senses.why: When nothing is shared between two things, people say they differ completely, so the word also covers whole extent.
senses.whyCN: 当两个事物没有任何共同点时，人们说它们完全不同，所以这个词也表示范围上的全部。

senses.title: Used to emphasize a state or feeling
senses.definition: used before adjectives or verbs to make the meaning stronger
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词或动词前加强语气
senses.example: I completely forgot to bring my homework.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全忘了带作业。
senses.why: Because the word means without exception, it becomes a natural way to stress how total a feeling or mistake is.
senses.whyCN: 因为它表示毫无例外，所以成了强调感受或错误有多彻底的自然说法。

intro.en: Completely is built from Latin parts that mean to fill up.
intro.cn: completely 由拉丁语词根构成，本义是「填满」。

items.en: The Latin verb complere meant to fill up or finish, from com- (with) + plere (to fill).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 complere 意为填满、完成，由 com-（一起）+ plere（填）构成。

items.en: Old French turned complere into complir, meaning to carry out.
items.cn: 古法语把 complere 变成 complir，意为执行、实现。

items.en: English adopted complete in the fourteenth century as an adjective meaning finished.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 complete 作形容词，意为完成的。

items.en: The adverb completely appeared soon after, meaning wholly or totally.
items.cn: 副词 completely 随后出现，意为完全地、彻底地。

items.en: Today completely is one of the most common intensifiers in spoken English.
items.cn: 如今 completely 是英语口语中最常用的强调副词之一。

note.en: These words are all built on the complete family or express totality.
note.cn: 这些词都属于 complete 词族，或同样表达「全部」的概念。

entries.definition: a nice thing you say to someone; note the i, different root
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；赞美（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: combining well to make a whole
entries.definitionCN: 互补的（与 complete 同源于 complere）

normalIntro.en: Link completely to the complete family.
normalIntro.cn: 把 completely 和 complete 词族连起来记。

normal.en: complete = com- (with) + plere (to fill).
normal.cn: complete 由 com- 加 plere 构成，意为填满。

normal.en: completely = complete + -ly, turning an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: completely 由 complete 加 -ly 构成，形容词变副词。

normal.en: complete homework = finish every question.
normal.cn: complete 作动词指把作业每道题都做完。

normal.en: completely full means nothing more can go in.
normal.cn: completely full 指再也装不进任何东西。

normal.en: completely sounds like come-please; come in, please fill it completely.
normal.cn: completely 发音像 come-please，进来吧，请把它装满。

abstract.en: Picture a glass filled to the very top rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一个杯子装到最顶端的边沿。

abstract.en: Picture wiping a blackboard so clean that no chalk marks remain.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板被擦得干干净净，一点粉笔印都没有。

abstract.en: Picture crossing out a whole page of wrong answers at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一次性划掉整页错误答案。

examples.en: The classroom was completely quiet during the test.
examples.cn: 考试期间教室里完全安静。

examples.en: I completely forgot about the basketball practice yesterday.
examples.cn: 我昨天完全忘了有篮球训练。

examples.en: Your new hairstyle makes you look completely different.
examples.cn: 你的新发型让你看起来完全不一样了。

sensesIntro.en: From filled-up to all-the-way and emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「填满」引申到「全然」再到「强调」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: filled up with nothing left

The image of filling supports the stress use.
branches.cn: 填满的意象支撑了强调用法。

latinIntro.cn: 词根 plere 意为填满，它填满了许多英语词。

definition_zh: 自信的；确信的；有把握的
definition_en: feeling sure that you can do something or that something is true
core_image: 站上台前深呼吸，心里稳稳地相信自己能做到
scene: 演讲比赛前，小华对着镜子练习了十几遍。After all that practice, she felt confident on the stage.
sceneCN: 这里 confident 是「自信的」（第 1 个义项：相信自己能做好）；句意是练习充分让她在台上很有信心。

derivatives.zh: 由 confident 加名词后缀构成，义为「信心；信任」
由 confident 加 -ly 构成，义为「自信地」
由同一词根构成，义为「机密的」

senses.title: Sure that you can do something
senses.definition: believing that you are able to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 相信自己能把某事做好
senses.example: He felt confident before the English speech contest.
senses.exampleCN: 英语演讲比赛前他感到很有信心。
senses.why: The Latin root means to trust fully, and trusting yourself gives the feeling of confidence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义是完全信任，信任自己便生出自信的感觉。

senses.title: Certain that something is true
senses.definition: being certain that something will happen or is true
senses.definitionCN: 确信某事会发生或是真的
senses.example: The scientists are confident that the plan will work.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家们确信这个计划会成功。
senses.why: The same trust turns outward: when you trust the facts, you are confident about the truth.
senses.whyCN: 同样的信任转向外部：当你相信事实，你便对真相确信不疑。

senses.title: Showing belief in yourself
senses.definition: behaving in a way that shows you believe in yourself
senses.definitionCN: 举止表现出相信自己的样子
senses.example: She walked into the classroom with a confident smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着自信的微笑走进教室。
senses.why: Inner belief shows on the outside, so confident also describes a look or manner.
senses.whyCN: 内心的信念会显露在外，所以 confident 也形容神态举止。

intro.en: Confident comes from Latin words meaning to trust fully.
intro.cn: confident 来自拉丁语，本义是「完全信任」。

items.en: The Latin verb confidere meant to trust fully, from con- (fully) + fidere (to trust).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 confidere 意为完全信任，由 con-（完全）+ fidere（信任）构成。

items.en: The related noun fiducia meant trust, the ancestor of confidence.
items.cn: 相关名词 fiducia 意为信任，是 confidence 的祖先。

items.en: French carried the idea into confident, meaning trusting.
items.cn: 法语把这一概念带入 confident，意为信任的。

items.en: English adopted confident in the fifteenth century, first about trusting people.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 confident，最初指信任他人。

items.en: Later the meaning moved to self-belief, and confidence became a common noun.
items.cn: 后来词义转向自我信念，confidence 也成了常用名词。

note.en: All these words grow from the Latin root fidere, to trust.
note.cn: 这些词都生长自拉丁词根 fidere（信任）。

secret; meant to be kept trusted and private
to tell a secret to someone you trust
a person you trust with your secrets
shy and lacking confidence; the di- prefix turns the meaning around

normal.en: diffident adds di- (away) and means not confident.
normal.cn: diffident 加 di-（离开）表示不自信。

normal.en: confident sounds like can-find-ent; you can find your courage.
normal.cn: confident 发音像 can-find-ent，你能找到自己的勇气。

examples.cn: 我确信我们队会赢得接力赛。

examples.en: Practice every day and you will become more confident in English.
examples.cn: 每天练习，你的英语会越来越有信心。

definition_en: to tell someone you are pleased about their success or good luck
core_image: 鼓着掌走向领奖的同学，大声说声恭喜
scene: 小林在作文比赛中得了一等奖，全班都为他高兴。We all congratulated him after the results were announced.
sceneCN: 这里 congratulate 是「祝贺」（第 1 个义项：向成功者表达高兴）；句意是成绩公布后大家都向他道贺。

derivatives.zh: 由 congratulate 加 -ion 构成，义为「祝贺；贺词」，常用复数 congratulations
由 congratulate 加 -ory 构成，义为「祝贺的」

senses.title: To express joy at someone's success
senses.titleCN: 为别人的成功表达喜悦
senses.definition: to say you are pleased about someone's success or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的成功或成就表示高兴
senses.example: The teacher congratulated us on winning the basketball final.
senses.exampleCN: 老师祝贺我们赢得篮球决赛。
senses.why: The Latin root means to rejoice together, so congratulating is sharing another person's joy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义是一同高兴，所以祝贺就是分享他人的喜悦。

senses.title: To praise someone for good luck or an event
senses.definition: to offer good words about a happy event such as a birth or a promotion
senses.definitionCN: 对喜事如升学、升职等送上祝福
senses.example: Everyone congratulated her when she passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过考试时大家都向她道贺。
senses.why: Happy events invite shared joy, and the verb covers these everyday celebrations too.
senses.whyCN: 喜事让人想一同庆祝，这个词也覆盖这些日常的庆祝场合。

senses.title: To express sympathy about avoiding trouble
senses.titleCN: 庆幸；为躲过麻烦而道贺
senses.definition: to say someone was lucky to avoid something bad
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人幸运地躲过了坏事
senses.example: I congratulated myself on catching the early bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我庆幸自己赶上了早班车。
senses.why: Sharing joy works both ways: you can even rejoice with yourself over a narrow escape.
senses.whyCN: 分享喜悦是双向的：甚至可以为自己躲过一劫而暗自庆幸。

intro.en: Congratulate literally means to rejoice together with someone.
intro.cn: congratulate 字面意思是「与某人一同欢乐」。

items.en: The Latin verb congratulari meant to rejoice with, from gratus (pleasing) + com- (with).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 congratulari 意为与人同乐，由 gratus（令人高兴）+ com-（共同）构成。

items.en: Medieval scholars used congratulatio for the act of expressing joy.
items.cn: 中世纪学者用 congratulatio 表示表达喜悦的行为。

items.en: French carried congratulacion into the language of scholars.
items.cn: 法语把 congratulacion 带进了学术语言。

items.en: English adopted congratulate in the sixteenth century as a learned word.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 congratulate，当时是书面用词。

items.en: Today it is a polite everyday verb, and congratulations is a common cheer.
items.cn: 如今它是礼貌的日常动词，congratulations 更成了常用的喝彩语。

note.en: These words share the grat root of joy, or mark similar celebrations.
note.cn: 这些词共享表示「高兴」的 grat 词根，或表示类似的祝贺。

definition_en: a competition; to compete for something or argue against it
core_image: 两个班级各划一条龙舟，鼓声里争着冲过终点
scene: 学校运动会报名开始了，五班和三班都想拿接力第一。Both classes will contest the relay final this Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 contest 是动词「争夺」（第 3 个义项：为赢得某物而竞争）；句意是两个班都要争夺接力决赛的名次。

参加比赛的人

senses.title: A competition with prizes
senses.definition: an event in which people compete to win something
senses.definitionCN: 人们为赢得某物而竞争的活动
senses.example: She won first prize in the school handwriting contest.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校书法比赛中获得一等奖。
senses.why: Latin testis means a witness, and judges witness who does best, naming the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 testis 意为证人，评委见证谁表现最好，于是给活动命名。

senses.title: A struggle against others
senses.definition: a fight or struggle to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而进行的较量
senses.example: The contest for the class monitor seat was close.
senses.exampleCN: 班长职位的竞争很激烈。
senses.why: The same image of rivals facing judges extends to any struggle for a goal.
senses.whyCN: 竞争对手面对评判者的画面延伸到一切争夺目标的行为。

senses.title: To compete or fight for something
senses.definition: to try hard to win something or beat others
senses.definitionCN: 努力赢得某物或战胜他人
senses.example: Twelve runners will contest the hundred-metre final.
senses.exampleCN: 十二名选手将角逐百米决赛。
senses.why: As a verb the word keeps its Latin force: to bring the matter before the contest.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时保留了拉丁语的力量：把事情摆上竞技场。

senses.title: To argue that something is wrong
senses.definition: to say formally that a decision or result is wrong and should be changed
senses.definitionCN: 正式表示某决定或结果有误
senses.example: Our team contested the referee's decision after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 赛后我们队对裁判的判罚提出了异议。
senses.why: You treat the decision like a rival you must fight in front of witnesses.
senses.whyCN: 你把那个决定当成必须在证人面前击败的对手。

intro.en: Contest goes back to Latin words about calling witnesses.
intro.cn: contest 可以追溯到拉丁语中「召唤证人」的用法。

items.en: The Latin verb contestari meant to call witnesses, from com- (together) + testari (to bear witness).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 contestari 意为召唤证人，由 com-（共同）+ testari（作证）构成。

items.en: Witnesses were called when two sides brought a dispute before a judge.
items.cn: 双方把争端提交法官时需要召唤证人。

items.en: Old French turned the legal word into contest, to dispute.
items.cn: 古法语把这个法律词变成 contest，意为争论。

items.en: English adopted contest in the sixteenth century for verbal disputes.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 contest，指言语争论。

items.en: Later the focus shifted from arguing to competing, giving today's senses.
items.cn: 后来词义焦点从争吵转向竞争，形成如今的各义项。

note.en: These words share the test/witness root or describe contests.
note.cn: 这些词共享 test（见证）词根，或描述各类竞赛。

entries.definition: a person taking part in a contest
an exam or trial; the witness root hides inside
entries.definitionCN: 测验；考试（同含见证词根）

entries.definition: to state that something is true
to give evidence as a witness
to say publicly that you are against something
an activity with rules for fun or winning

normalIntro.en: Remember the witness root inside contest.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 contest 里藏着「见证」词根。

normal.en: contest = com- (together) + testari (to witness).
normal.cn: contest 由 com-（共同）+ testari（作证）构成。

normal.en: protest has the same root and means to speak against.
normal.cn: protest 同根，意为反对。

normal.en: attest and testify keep the witness meaning clearly.
normal.cn: attest 和 testify 清楚保留了见证之义。

normal.en: contestant = contest + -ant, the person who contests.
normal.cn: contestant 由 contest 加 -ant 构成，即参赛者。

normal.en: contest sounds like kon-test; rivals meet one big test.
normal.cn: contest 发音像 kon-test，对手相遇同考一场大试。

abstract.en: Picture two teams facing a judge at the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象两队在终点线面对裁判。

abstract.en: Picture a stage with bright lights and a prize table.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光闪烁的舞台和奖品桌。

abstract.en: Picture raising your hand to question a result.
abstract.cn: 想象举手对结果提出质疑。

examples.en: Our class entered the English speech contest last month.
examples.cn: 我们班上个月报名了英语演讲比赛。

examples.en: Three schools will contest the city football title.
examples.cn: 三所学校将争夺市足球冠军。

examples.en: He contested the judge's score, but the result stood.
examples.cn: 他对裁判的评分提出异议，但结果没有改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扛台赛」——扛着奖杯上台领奖，因为赢了这场比赛。

root: 拉丁语 contestari（召唤证人作证），由 com-（共同）+ testari（作证）构成。test 词根同族词有 protest（抗议）、attest（证明）、testify（作证）。

sensesIntro.en: From calling witnesses to competing and objecting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从召唤证人延伸到竞技与异议。

core.cn: 核心意象：对手在见证者面前较量

branches.en: Decisions can be witnessed and disputed.
branches.cn: 结果可被见证也可被质疑。

intro.en: The test root of witnessing shapes several argument words.
intro.cn: test（见证）词根塑造了若干表示争论的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin testari means to bear witness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 testari 意为作证。

items.example: The twins cooperated in the race.
The judge listened to every witness.
items.exampleCN: 法官听取了每位证人的陈述。
每位参赛者抽了一个号码。

items.example: Two teachers can attest to his honesty.
items.exampleCN: 两位老师可以证实他的诚实。

items.example: She testified in the school court.
Her medals are a testament to hard work.
items.exampleCN: 她的奖牌是努力的证明。

definition_en: useful and easy for you, causing no trouble
core_image: 楼下的便利店，出门三步就能买到东西
scene: 新学期教室搬到了操场旁边，下课去图书馆更近了。The new building is very convenient for students.
sceneCN: 这里 convenient 是「便利的」（第 1 个义项：省事、不添麻烦）；句意是新楼对学生来说很方便。

derivatives.zh: 由 convenient 加名词后缀构成，义为「便利；方便」
由 convenient 加 -ly 构成，义为「方便地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不方便的」

senses.title: Easy to use or reach
senses.definition: useful because it saves you time or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 因省时省事而有用的
senses.example: The bus stop near our school is very convenient.
senses.exampleCN: 学校附近的公交站很方便。
senses.why: Latin venire means to come, and something convenient comes easily to meet your needs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venire 意为来到，便利之物轻松「来到」满足你的需要。

senses.title: Suitable; happening at the right time
senses.definition: fitting well with your plans or schedule
senses.definitionCN: 与你的计划或安排很契合
senses.example: Friday afternoon is a convenient time for our group meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 周五下午开小组会时间很合适。
senses.why: When things come together at the right moment, no one is troubled, so convenient also means suitable.
senses.whyCN: 事物恰好在合适的时刻齐聚，谁都不添麻烦，所以 convenient 也表示合适。

senses.title: Close by; handy in position
senses.definition: located near enough to be easy to use
senses.definitionCN: 位置足够近、用起来省事
senses.example: Our new flat is convenient to both the school and the park.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的新家离学校和公园都近。
senses.why: A place that comes close to you saves the journey, extending coming to location.
senses.whyCN: 离你近的地方省去了路途，把「来到」延伸到位置上。

intro.en: Convenient comes from Latin words about coming together.
intro.cn: convenient 来自拉丁语中「聚到一起」的表达。

items.en: The Latin verb convenire meant to come together or agree, from com- (together) + venire (to come).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 convenire 意为聚在一起、一致，由 com-（共同）+ venire（来）构成。

items.en: The participle conveniens described things that fit well together.
items.cn: 分词 conveniens 形容彼此契合的事物。

items.en: French carried convenant and related forms meaning to agree.
items.cn: 法语用 convenant 及相关形式表示约定、同意。

items.en: English adopted convenient in the fourteenth century, first meaning agreeing or fitting.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 convenient，最初意为相合、契合。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the main meaning had moved to easy and useful.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义主流转向省事、有用。

note.en: These words share the ven root of coming, or mean easy to use.
note.cn: 这些词共享 ven（来）词根，或表示易用。

entries.definition: the quality of being easy and useful
to gather people for a meeting
to come between and change a situation
a building for nuns; one letter different, same root family
entries.definitionCN: 女修道院（拼写相近，同根不同义）

entries.definition: something newly made; close spelling but different root
entries.definitionCN: 发明（拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: Link convenient to the coming-together root ven.
normalIntro.cn: 把 convenient 和表示「来」的 ven 词根连起来记。

normal.en: convenient = com- (together) + venire (to come).
normal.cn: convenient 由 com-（共同）+ venire（来）构成。

normal.en: convene and intervention keep the ven root.
normal.cn: convene 和 intervention 都保留 ven 词根。

normal.en: convenience is the noun; a convenience store is handy.
normal.cn: convenience 是名词；便利店就是 handy 的店。

normal.en: in- makes inconvenient, the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 in- 构成 inconvenient，反义词。

normal.en: convenient sounds like can-ve-nyent; you can go there any moment.
normal.cn: convenient 发音像 can-ve-nyent，你随时都能去。

abstract.en: Picture a shop right next to the school gate.
abstract.cn: 想象紧挨校门的小店。

abstract.en: Picture your timetable and a meeting slot clicking together like puzzle pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象课程表和会议时段像拼图一样契合。

abstract.en: Picture stepping out of the lift right at your front door.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯门一开正好是家门口。

examples.en: It is convenient to take the subway to the museum.
examples.cn: 坐地铁去博物馆很方便。

examples.en: Please choose a convenient time for our video call.
examples.cn: 请选一个方便的时间视频通话。

examples.en: The convenience store near my home opens all night.
examples.cn: 我家附近的便利店通宵营业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯为你而特」——这家店肯为你特设窗口，办事真方便。

root: 拉丁语 convenire（聚到一起；一致），由 com-（共同）+ venire（来）构成。ven 词根同族词有 convene（召集）、intervene（介入）、event（事件）。

sensesIntro.en: From coming together to easy, suitable and nearby.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「聚到一起」引申为省事、合适与近便。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things coming together easily
core.cn: 核心意象：事物轻松聚拢

branches.en: Fit and place both save trouble.

intro.en: The ven root of coming travels through many English words.
intro.cn: 表示「来」的 ven 词根出现在许多英语词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire means to come.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire 意为来。

items.example: The class convened for a meeting.
The next event is sports day.
The teacher intervened to stop the argument.
The parade marched down the avenue.

definition_en: an informal talk in which people exchange news and feelings
core_image: 两个人面对面，你一句我一句像打乒乓球
scene: 午休时，我和同桌聊起周末的机器人展览。Our conversation about robots lasted the whole lunch break.
sceneCN: 这里 conversation 是「交谈」（第 1 个义项：两人轮流说话交流）；句意是我们关于机器人的谈话聊了整个午休。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根构成，义为「交谈」
由 conversation 加 -al 构成，义为「口语的；健谈的」
义为「用谈话方式」

senses.title: An informal talk between people
senses.definition: a talk in which people share news, ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 人们交流消息、想法或感受的谈话
senses.example: I had a long conversation with my grandma on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 我和奶奶在电话里聊了很久。
senses.why: Latin versare means to turn, and a conversation turns from speaker to speaker like a wheel.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 versare 意为转动，交谈像轮子一样在说话人之间轮转。

senses.title: The skill or style of talking
senses.definition: the way someone talks with others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人与人交谈的方式
senses.example: Good conversation makes parties more fun.
senses.exampleCN: 好的谈吐让聚会更有趣。
senses.why: Because talks rotate smoothly, the word also names the manner of the exchange itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于谈话轮转顺畅，这个词也指交流本身的方式。

senses.title: A formal exchange in computing
senses.definition: an exchange between a user and a program or system
senses.definitionCN: 用户与程序系统之间的交互
senses.example: The app keeps a conversation history of your questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用保存你的问答记录。
senses.why: Machine dialogue imitates human turn-taking, so engineers borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 机器对话模仿人类轮流说话，工程师便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Conversation originally meant the act of turning about or living among people.
intro.cn: conversation 最初意为「转身往复；与人共处」。

items.en: The Latin verb conversari meant to live with or keep company, from com- (with) + versare (to turn often).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 conversari 意为与人共处，由 com-（与）+ versare（反复转动）构成。

items.en: conversatio described one's manner of life and behaviour.
items.cn: conversatio 描述一个人的生活方式与举止。

items.en: French carried conversacion with meanings of conduct and company.
items.cn: 法语 conversacion 兼有行为与交往之义。

items.en: English first used conversation for conduct and later for living together.
items.cn: 英语最初用 conversation 表示行为，后指与人交往。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it meant the familiar exchange of words we know today.
items.cn: 到十七世纪它才表示今天熟悉的言谈交流。

note.en: These words share the vers root of turning, or name kinds of talk.
note.cn: 这些词共享 vers（转）词根，或表示各种言谈。

entries.definition: to talk with someone; also an opposite noun
a public argument; close spelling, different root
entries.definitionCN: 争论；争议（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: protecting nature; only the letters differ
entries.definitionCN: 保护；节约（与 conversation 拼写易混，词源不同）

entries.definition: talk between two people or sides
talk to examine a topic seriously
the general act of speaking together

normalIntro.en: Remember the turning root inside conversation.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 conversation 里的「转动」词根。

normal.en: conversation = com- (with) + versare (to turn).
normal.cn: conversation 由 com-（与）+ versare（转动）构成。

normal.en: vers is the turning root in reverse and universe.
normal.cn: vers 是转动词根，见于 reverse 和 universe。

normal.en: converse is the verb for having a conversation.
normal.cn: converse 是表示交谈的动词。

normal.en: conservation looks similar but protects nature.
normal.cn: conservation 拼写相似但意为保护自然。

normal.en: conversation sounds like kon-ver-say-shun; we turn and say, turn and say.
normal.cn: conversation 发音像 kon-ver-say-shun，转过来你说，转过去我说。

abstract.en: Picture a ping-pong ball of words flying back and forth.
abstract.cn: 想象话语像乒乓球来回飞。

abstract.en: Picture two friends on a bench, laughing in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象长椅上两个朋友轮流大笑。

abstract.en: Picture a spinning wheel passing the turn to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象转盘把说话机会传给下一个人。

examples.en: We had a short conversation before the English class.
examples.cn: 英语课前我们简短地聊了几句。

examples.en: She started a conversation with the new student.
examples.cn: 她主动和新同学攀谈起来。

examples.en: Practise conversations with your partner to improve spoken English.
examples.cn: 和同伴练习对话来提高英语口语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯我色身」——肯对我笑着搭话（色身谐音生人），原来是想和我交谈。

root: 拉丁语 conversari（与人共处），由 com-（与）+ versare（反复转动）构成。vers 词根同族词有 converse（交谈）、reverse（逆转）、universe（宇宙）。

sensesIntro.en: From living together to talking and turn-taking.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「与人共处」引申为交谈与轮替。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words turning from one to another
core.cn: 核心意象：话语在人们之间轮转

branches.en: Sharing news in a casual talk.
A user and a system taking turns.

branches.cn: 好的谈话是顺畅的轮转。

intro.en: The vers root of turning spins through a big word family.
intro.cn: 表示「转动」的 vers 词根旋转出一大族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin versare means to turn again and again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 versare 意为反复转动。

items.example: We compiled a class dictionary together.
The earth revolves around the sun.
Our class is diverse in hobbies.

definition_en: to prepare food by heating it; a person who cooks
core_image: 系上围裙站在灶台前，锅里咕嘟咕嘟冒热气
scene: 周末妈妈教我做西红柿炒蛋，油烟机嗡嗡地响。My mother taught me how to cook this simple dish.
sceneCN: 这里 cook 是动词「烹调」（第 1 个义项：加热做食物）；句意是妈妈教我做这道简单的菜。

derivatives.zh: 由 cook 加 -er 构成，义为「炊具（英式）」
由 cook 加 -ing 构成，义为「烹饪；烹调术」
cook 与 book 合成，义为「食谱」
法语借词，义为「（专业）厨师」

senses.title: To prepare food with heat
senses.definition: to prepare food by heating it, for example boiling or frying
senses.definitionCN: 用加热的方式做食物，如煮、炒
senses.example: I can cook fried rice with eggs and vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 我会做蛋炒饭加蔬菜。
senses.why: The core image is changing raw food into a meal with heat.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是用火把生食材变成饭菜。

senses.title: To work as the person making meals
senses.definition: to prepare food as a job
senses.definitionCN: 以做饭为职业
senses.example: My uncle cooks at a restaurant near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔在车站附近的一家餐馆当厨师。
senses.why: When cooking becomes daily work, the verb names the job too.
senses.whyCN: 当做饭变成日常工作，这个动词也指这份职业。

senses.title: A person who prepares food
senses.definition: someone who cooks meals, especially as a job
senses.definitionCN: 做饭的人，尤指以此为业
senses.example: The school cook makes wonderful dumplings.
senses.exampleCN: 学校厨师做的饺子特别棒。
senses.why: English often turns action verbs into names for people who do them.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动词转成做这件事的人的称呼。

senses.title: To be cooking or heating up
senses.definition: to be heated so that it is getting ready to eat
senses.definitionCN: 正被加热到可以吃的程度
senses.example: The soup is still cooking on the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 汤还在炉子上炖着。
senses.why: Food itself can sit in the state of cooking, so the verb also works without an object.
senses.whyCN: 食物本身可以处于烹制状态，所以动词也可以不带宾语。

intro.en: Cook is one of the oldest English food words, from Latin coquere.
intro.cn: cook 是英语最古老的饮食词之一，源自拉丁语 coquere。

items.en: The Latin verb coquere meant to cook or ripen, from the Indo-European root pekw- meaning to cook or ripen.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 coquere 意为烹煮、使成熟，来自印欧词根 pekw-（煮、熟）。

items.en: Germanic peoples borrowed the word as kok-, giving Dutch kok and German Koch.
items.cn: 日耳曼各语言借入该词成为 kok-，衍生出荷兰语 kok 和德语 Koch。

items.en: Old English had coc as both the cook and the cooking.
items.cn: 古英语的 coc 既指厨师也指烹煮。

items.en: The spelling settled as cook, covering the person and the action.
items.cn: 中世纪英语拼法定为 cook，兼指人与动作。

items.en: Modern English added cooker, cookbook and cooking as a noun.
items.cn: 现代英语又派生出 cooker、cookbook 以及名词 cooking。

note.en: These words come from the Latin cooking root coqu-, or name kitchen things.
note.cn: 这些词源自拉丁语烹煮词根 coqu-，或与厨房事物相关。

entries.definition: a device for cooking, in British English
a male chicken; one letter changes the meaning
entries.definitionCN: 公鸡（拼写相近，词义无关）

entries.definition: a small sweet flat cake; from the same Dutch cooking word
entries.definitionCN: 曲奇饼（源自同一荷兰语烹煮词）

entries.definition: a professional cook, especially in a restaurant
to cook food in an oven without liquid
to cook in very hot bubbling water

normalIntro.en: Cook is short and old, easy to keep in mind.
normalIntro.cn: cook 又短又古老，很好记。

normal.en: cook comes from Latin coquere, to cook.
normal.cn: cook 源自拉丁语 coquere，意为烹煮。

normal.en: cooker is the machine; cook is the person.
normal.cn: cooker 是炊具；cook 是人。

normal.en: cookie came from Dutch koekje, a little cake.
normal.cn: cookie 来自荷兰语 koekje，小点心。

normal.en: cookbook = cook + book, a book of recipes.
normal.cn: cookbook 由 cook 加 book 构成，食谱书。

normal.en: cook sounds like the name Cook; a chef named Cook runs the kitchen.
normal.cn: cook 发音像「库克」，想象名叫库克的大厨掌管厨房。

abstract.cn: 想象一锅面条冒着热气。

abstract.en: Picture a white hat and apron in a school kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象学校厨房里的白帽子和围裙。

abstract.en: Picture rice bubbling quietly on a small fire.
abstract.cn: 想象小火上咕嘟作响的米饭。

examples.en: My father cooks dinner for the family every Friday.
examples.cn: 每周五爸爸都为全家做晚饭。

examples.en: The cook prepared vegetable soup for the school canteen.
examples.cn: 厨师为学校食堂做了蔬菜汤。

examples.en: Learning to cook simple meals makes you more independent.
examples.cn: 学会做简单的饭菜会让你更独立。

sensesIntro.en: From heating food to the person and the job.
sensesIntro.cn: 从加热食物延伸到职业与人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: turning raw food into a meal with heat
core.cn: 核心意象：用火把生食材变成饭菜

branches.en: Food in the state of cooking.
The pot keeps working until done.
branches.cn: 锅一直在工作直到做好。

intro.en: The coqu root of cooking flavor English food words.
intro.cn: coqu（烹煮）词根滋养了英语的饮食词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin coquere means to cook.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 coquere 意为烹煮。

items.example: The kitchen is where we cook.
items.exampleCN: 厨房是我们做饭的地方。

definition_en: a small flat sweet cake, often crisp
core_image: 烤盘上金黄的小圆饼，还带着巧克力的香气
scene: 烘焙课上，同学们把面团压成小圆片送进烤箱。Soon the classroom smelled of warm chocolate cookies.
sceneCN: 这里 cookie 是「曲奇饼」（第 1 个义项：扁平的小甜饼）；句意是不久教室里弥漫着热巧克力和曲奇的香味。

senses.title: A small flat sweet cake
senses.definition: a small, flat, usually sweet baked cake
senses.definitionCN: 通常扁平带甜味的小块烘焙点心
senses.example: She baked peanut cookies for the class party.
senses.exampleCN: 她为班级聚会烤了花生曲奇。
senses.why: The Dutch made koekje, a little cake, and English borrowed the word for this snack.
senses.whyCN: 荷兰人称小蛋糕为 koekje，英语借来指这种点心。

senses.title: A person or thing of a stated type
senses.definition: a person or thing of a particular kind, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指某类人或物
senses.example: He is one smart cookie in maths.
senses.exampleCN: 他是数学上相当机灵的一个小子。
senses.why: A cookie is one whole piece, so people use it to mean one whole person of a kind.
senses.whyCN: 曲奇是一块完整的点心，人们借此指某一类人中的一员。

senses.title: A small file a website saves
senses.titleCN: （计算机）存储在浏览器中的信息
senses.definition: a small file that a website stores in your browser
senses.definitionCN: 网站存到你浏览器里的小文件
senses.example: The website uses cookies to remember your login.
senses.exampleCN: 该网站用 cookies 记住你的登录信息。
senses.why: A cookie keeps a small trace of you, just like a treat left in the jar.
senses.whyCN: cookie 留下一点关于你的痕迹，就像罐子里留下的一块点心。

intro.en: Cookie is a Dutch word for a little cake that crossed the sea.
intro.cn: cookie 是漂洋过海而来的荷兰语「小蛋糕」。

items.en: Dutch koekje, a diminutive of koek (cake), meant a little cake.
items.cn: 荷兰语 koekje 是 koek（蛋糕）的指小形式，意为小蛋糕。

items.en: The Dutch word goes back to Germanic roots shared with cook.
items.cn: 荷兰语该词与 cook 共享日耳曼词根。

items.en: Related forms appear in Scandinavian languages for little baked cakes.
items.cn: 相关形式也出现在斯堪的纳维亚语言中，指小点心。

items.en: American settlers brought koekje, which became cookie in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 美洲移民带来 koekje，十八世纪演变为 cookie。

items.en: British English kept biscuit, while cookie became the American favourite.
items.cn: 英式英语保留了 biscuit，cookie 成为美式最爱。

note.en: These words are cookie's cousins or close rivals in the biscuit family.
note.cn: 这些词是 cookie 的表亲或饼干家族的近亲。

entries.definition: a cooking machine, not a cake
entries.definitionCN: 炊具（拼写相近，词义不同）

entries.definition: the verb or person of cooking
the British word for a similar sweet snack
the British word for a small sweet flat snack
sweet baked food made from dough

normalIntro.en: Cookie hides the cook inside.
normalIntro.cn: cookie 里藏着 cook。

normal.en: cookie = cook + ie, a little cooked cake.
normal.cn: cookie 由 cook 加指小后缀构成，小蛋糕。

normal.en: Dutch koekje means a little cake.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 koekje 意为小蛋糕。

normal.en: British biscuit is the same snack.
normal.cn: 英式 biscuit 是同样的点心。

normal.en: a smart cookie means a clever person.
normal.cn: a smart cookie 指聪明人。

normal.en: cookie sounds like cool-key; a cookie is a cool little treat-key.
normal.cn: cookie 发音像 cool-key，想象一把能打开甜品罐的酷酷小钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a jar full of round golden cookies.
abstract.cn: 想象装满金黄圆曲奇的罐子。

abstract.en: Picture crumbs falling from your first bite.
abstract.cn: 想象咬下第一口时掉下的碎屑。

abstract.en: Picture Santa's plate of cookies on Christmas Eve.
abstract.cn: 想象圣诞夜给圣诞老人准备的曲奇盘。

examples.en: We exchanged cookies at the class New Year party.
examples.cn: 班级新年聚会上我们交换了曲奇。

examples.en: Grandma's chocolate chip cookies are the best in our family.
examples.cn: 奶奶的巧克力豆曲奇是全家最好吃的。

examples.en: Remember to clear the cookies if the login fails.
examples.cn: 如果登录失败，记得清除 cookies。

sensesIntro.en: From a small cake to a clever person and a web file.
sensesIntro.cn: 从小蛋糕引申到机灵鬼和网络文件。

core.cn: 核心意象：一块小小的圆形甜点

branches.cn: 完整的一块代指完整的人。

intro.cn: cook 词根展示小物件如何获得「小」后缀。

latinIntro.cn: 荷兰语指小后缀 -je 表示「小」。

definition_zh: 凉的；凉爽的；冷静的；酷的
definition_en: slightly cold; calm; very good or fashionable
core_image: 冰镇汽水瓶上滑落的水珠，凉意刚好
scene: 体育课后，饮料机里刚拿出的汽水让全班都围了过来。A cool drink after sports feels wonderful.
sceneCN: 这里 cool 是「凉爽的」（第 1 个义项：温度略低、令人舒服）；句意是运动后喝一瓶凉饮料真舒服。

derivatives.zh: 由 cool 加 -ly 构成，义为「冷静地；酷酷地」
由 cool 加 -er 构成，义为「冷藏箱（美式）」
由 cool 加 -ness 构成，义为「凉爽；冷静」

senses.title: Slightly cold in a pleasant way
senses.definition: a little cold, often in a pleasant or refreshing way
senses.definitionCN: 温度略低，常给人舒服清爽之感
senses.example: A cool wind blew across the playground in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 早晨一阵凉风吹过操场。
senses.why: Cool sits between hot and cold, a temperature that comforts the body.
senses.whyCN: cool 位于热与冷之间，是让身体舒适的温度。

senses.title: Calm and not excited
senses.definition: staying calm and not getting angry or excited
senses.definitionCN: 保持平静，不激动不生气
senses.example: She kept a cool head when the fire alarm rang.
senses.exampleCN: 火警响起时她保持冷静。
senses.why: Low temperature suggests low emotion, so cool people keep their feelings down.
senses.whyCN: 低温联想低情绪，所以冷静的人情绪平稳。

senses.title: Very good; fashionable
senses.definition: excellent, attractive or fashionable, especially in youth speech
senses.definitionCN: 出色的、有吸引力的或时髦的，常见于年轻人用语
senses.example: Your new skateboard is really cool!
senses.exampleCN: 你的新滑板真酷！
senses.why: A relaxed confident manner looks attractive, so cool became a word of praise.
senses.whyCN: 从容自信的姿态很有魅力，cool 于是成了赞美之词。

senses.title: To become or make something colder
senses.definition: to become colder or make something colder
senses.definitionCN: 变凉或使某物变凉
senses.example: Let the hot soup cool down before you drink it.
senses.exampleCN: 热汤先晾一晾再喝。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a verb: helping something reach that pleasant temperature.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成动词：让东西达到那舒适的温度。

senses.title: Unfriendly or distant
senses.definition: not friendly; showing little warmth or interest
senses.definitionCN: 不友好，缺少热情或兴趣
senses.example: He gave me a cool reply without a smile.
senses.exampleCN: 他面无笑容地冷冷回了我一句。
senses.why: Coldness of feeling echoes coldness of temperature, so cool can also mean distant.
senses.whyCN: 情感的冷呼应温度的冷，cool 也指态度疏远。

intro.en: Cool is an old Germanic word for a pleasant mild coldness.
intro.cn: cool 是古老的日耳曼词，指令人舒适的微凉。

items.en: The Germanic root kol- meant cool or cold, seen in German kuhl.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 kol- 意为凉的、冷的，见于德语 kuhl。

items.en: Old English col described both weather and feelings.
items.cn: 古英语 col 既描述天气也描述心境。

items.en: Norse kula and related forms travelled with the Vikings.
items.cn: 北欧语 kula 等相关形式随维京人传播。

items.en: Spelling fixed as cool in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪拼法固定为 cool。

items.en: In the twentieth century jazz culture turned cool into a word for style and approval.
items.cn: 二十世纪爵士文化把 cool 变成表示有型、赞许的词。

note.en: Some words share the cold family, others are cool's easy confusions.
note.cn: 有的词属于寒冷词族，有的则是 cool 的易混词。

entries.definition: colder than cool; a different strength of the same idea
entries.definitionCN: 冷的（比 cool 程度更深）

entries.definition: to prepare food; one letter changes everything
entries.definitionCN: 烹调（拼写相近，词义无关）

entries.definition: black fuel dug from the ground
an old word for a labourer; different root
a box that keeps drinks cold
lower than cool, icy and unpleasant
making you feel fresh and comfortable

normalIntro.en: Cool is one sound with many cool uses.
normalIntro.cn: cool 一个音，多种酷用法。

normal.en: cool weather sits between warm and cold.
normal.cn: cool 的天气介于暖和冷之间。

normal.en: keep cool means stay calm in trouble.
normal.cn: keep cool 指遇事保持冷静。

normal.en: cool also means excellent or fashionable.
normal.cn: cool 也表示很棒、很时髦。

normal.en: cool down lets hot food or angry people relax.
normal.cn: cool down 让热食降温、让生气的人平复。

normal.en: cool sounds like the Chinese word for cool; they share the meaning.
normal.cn: cool 与汉语的「酷」发音相近，意思也被汉语借用了。

abstract.en: Picture water drops sliding down a chilled bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象冰镇瓶壁滑落的水珠。

abstract.en: Picture a classmate calmly solving a hard maths problem.
abstract.cn: 想象同学冷静地解出一道难题。

abstract.en: Picture sunglasses and a skateboard under sunset light.
abstract.cn: 想象夕阳下滑板少年的墨镜。

examples.en: Aut mornings here are cool, so take a jacket.
examples.cn: 这里秋天的早晨很凉，带件外套吧。

examples.en: Stay cool and read the question twice before answering.
examples.cn: 保持冷静，答题前把题目读两遍。

examples.en: That song is so cool that everyone in our class hums it.
examples.cn: 那首歌太酷了，全班都在哼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「酷」——天气凉爽心情酷，遇事冷静更是酷。

root: 日耳曼词根 kol-（凉；冷），与德语 kuhl、荷兰语 koel 同源。cool 与 cold 同属寒冷语义场，但程度更温和。

sensesIntro.en: From mild coldness to calm, style and distance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从微凉引申到冷静、有型与冷淡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pleasant mild coldness
core.cn: 核心意象：恰到好处的微凉

intro.en: Cool is a single root that English bends into many shapes.
intro.cn: cool 是单一词根，英语把它弯出多种形态。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic, so there are no Latin relatives here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族属日耳曼源，没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: A chill ran down my back.

definition_zh: 复制；抄写；模仿；复印；本；册；副本
definition_en: to make something the same as an original; a single book or a reproduction
core_image: 复印机的光一遍遍扫过，吐出和原件一模一样的纸
scene: 美术课上同桌的星星画得特别好看，我不由得照着画了一张。I quietly copied her drawing of stars.
sceneCN: 这里 copy 是动词「模仿；照着画」（第 3 个义项：仿照原样制作）；句意是我悄悄照着她的星星画描了一张。

derivatives.zh: copy 与 book 合成，义为「习字帖」
由 copy 加 -ist 构成，义为「抄写员」
photo 与 copy 合成，义为「复印件」

senses.title: To make an exact reproduction
senses.definition: to make something exactly like the original
senses.definitionCN: 制作与原件一模一样的东西
senses.example: Please copy this page for everyone in the group.
senses.exampleCN: 请把这页复印给组里每个人。
senses.why: The core image is the machine that sends out twin pages.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是复印机吐出双胞胎纸页。

senses.title: To write out words from another source
senses.definition: to write the same words that you can see somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 照着某处可见的文字书写
senses.example: We copied the new words into our notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把生词抄进笔记本。
senses.why: Your hand follows the original line by line, a slower kind of copying.
senses.whyCN: 手一行行追随原件，是慢速的复制。

senses.title: To imitate someone or something
senses.definition: to do things the way another person does them
senses.definitionCN: 学着别人的样子做事
senses.example: Little brothers often copy what older ones do.
senses.exampleCN: 弟弟常模仿哥哥做的事。
senses.why: Imitation copies not paper but behaviour, the same idea applied to people.
senses.whyCN: 模仿复制的不是纸而是行为，是把同一概念用于人。

senses.title: A single book, newspaper or document
senses.definition: one single book, newspaper or document of many
senses.definitionCN: 许多相同书报中的一册
senses.example: There are only two copies of this magazine in the library.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆这本杂志只剩两本。
senses.why: Every printed book is a copy of one original text.
senses.whyCN: 每本印刷书都是某一原文本的复制品。

senses.title: A reproduction or duplicate
senses.definition: something made to be the same as an original
senses.definitionCN: 为与原件相同而做的东西
senses.example: Keep a copy of your ID card in your schoolbag.
senses.exampleCN: 书包里放一张身份证复印件。
senses.why: The noun names the twin itself, not the act.
senses.whyCN: 名词指那份孪生品，而非动作。

intro.en: Copy comes from Latin words about abundance, surprising as that sounds.
intro.cn: copy 出人意料地来自表示「充足」的拉丁词。

items.en: The Latin noun copia meant abundance or supply.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 copia 意为丰富、大量。

items.en: Writers used copia for the plenty of written material, giving the term copia libelli for a fair copy of a text.
items.cn: 作家用 copia 指大量文本，遂有 copia libelli 表示文本的誊清本。

items.en: Old French turned this into copie, a reproduction of a manuscript.
items.cn: 古法语变为 copie，指手稿的复本。

items.en: English adopted copy in the fourteenth century for written duplicates.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 copy，指书面复本。

items.en: With printing and machines, copy spread to books, files and even imitating people.
items.cn: 随着印刷与机器，copy 扩展到书刊、文件，甚至指模仿人。

note.en: Some words share the copia root, others copy copy's shape.
note.cn: 有的词共享 copia 词根，有的形似 copy。

咖啡（拼写相近，词义无关）

entries.definition: the legal right over an original work
entries.definitionCN: 版权（copy 与 right 合成）
复制品；完全相同的副本

an exact genetic or digital copy

normalIntro.en: Copy is twin-making in paper, ink and life.
normalIntro.cn: copy 是纸、墨和生活中的「孪生术」。

normal.en: copy comes from Latin copia, abundance of text.
normal.cn: copy 源自拉丁语 copia，文本之丰。

normal.en: copious shares the root and means plentiful.
normal.cn: copious 同根，意为大量的。

normal.en: copy the notes means write the same words.
normal.cn: copy the notes 指照抄同样的字。

normal.en: a copy of the book means one printed volume.
normal.cn: a copy of the book 指一册印刷书。

normal.en: copy sounds like copybei; typing copybei on a computer copies a file.
normal.cn: copy 音译为「拷贝」，在电脑上拷贝就是复制文件。

abstract.en: Picture the photocopier light sweeping across the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象复印机的光扫过玻璃板。

abstract.en: Picture two identical snowflakes side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象两片一模一样的雪花并排。

abstract.en: Picture a little brother walking behind his big brother.
abstract.cn: 想象弟弟跟在哥哥身后学走路。

examples.en: Please do not copy answers during the exam.
examples.cn: 考试时请不要抄答案。

examples.en: This dictionary has more than one million copies in print.
examples.cn: 这本词典印量超过一百万册。

examples.en: Artists sometimes copy the old masters to learn brushwork.
examples.cn: 画家有时临摹古代大师来学习笔法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拷倍」——拷贝一份，份数翻倍。

root: 拉丁语 copia（丰富；大量），先指文本的充足，后指誊清的复本。同根词 copious（大量的）保留「丰富」本义。

sensesIntro.en: From abundant text to twins in paper and behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「文本充足」延伸到纸面与行为上的孪生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: making a twin of the original
core.cn: 核心意象：为原件造一个孪生品

branches.en: The noun counts books and duplicates.
Twin-making works on things and people.
branches.cn: 孪生术既用于物也用于人。

intro.en: The cop root of plenty hides inside copy.
intro.cn: 表示「充足」的 cop 词根藏在 copy 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin copia means abundance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 copia 意为丰富。

definition_en: plants like wheat or maize grown for food; the seeds of these plants
core_image: 秋天的田野里，金黄的玉米棒排满垄间
scene: 秋游时同学们钻进玉米地掰玉米，笑声此起彼伏。The farmer let us pick fresh corn in the field.
sceneCN: 这里 corn 是「玉米」（第 2 个义项：美式指玉米作物）；句意是农民让我们在地里掰新鲜玉米。

derivatives.zh: corn 与 field 合成，义为「谷物田」
pop 与 corn 合成，义为「爆米花」
corn 与 flake 合成，义为「玉米片」

senses.title: Grain plants or their seeds
senses.definition: the seeds of grain plants such as wheat and barley, in British English
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语指小麦、大麦等谷物的种子
senses.example: The old mill ground corn into flour for bread.
senses.exampleCN: 老磨坊把谷物磨成面粉做面包。
senses.why: In Britain corn was the general word for the main local grain.
senses.whyCN: 在英国，corn 曾泛指当地主要谷物。

senses.title: Maize; the tall grain plant with yellow seeds
senses.definition: in American English, the maize plant and its yellow kernels
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语指玉米植株及黄色玉米粒
senses.example: We roasted corn on the cob at the school farm fair.
senses.exampleCN: 学校农场集市上我们烤了玉米棒。
senses.why: Settlers in America gave corn a new meaning: maize.
senses.whyCN: 美洲移民赋予 corn 新义：玉米。

senses.title: A small hard round area of skin
senses.definition: a small painful hard spot of skin, usually on a foot
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上小的硬痛点，多在脚上
senses.example: New shoes gave him a corn on his little toe.
senses.exampleCN: 新鞋让他小脚趾磨出了鸡眼。
senses.why: A corn looks like a hard yellow seed stuck on the skin.
senses.whyCN: 鸡眼看着像粘在皮肤上的硬黄谷粒。

intro.en: Corn is a Germanic word that once meant the seed of any grain.
intro.cn: corn 是日耳曼词，曾泛指任何谷物的种子。

items.en: The Germanic root korn- meant a small hard grain.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 korn- 意为细小坚硬的谷粒。

items.en: Norse korn shared the same seed meaning with Germanic speech.
items.cn: 北欧语 korn 与日耳曼语共有「种子」义。

items.en: Old English corn covered grain of any kind, whatever the region grew.
items.cn: 古英语 corn 泛指各类谷物，因地区而异。

items.en: British English kept the general grain meaning.

definition_en: the place where two lines, walls or streets meet
core_image: 两面墙相遇的那条线，扫帚总爱把灰尘扫到那里
scene: 放学后我在书店门口等人，书店就在十字路口附近。I stood waiting at the corner of the street.
sceneCN: 这里 corner 是「街角」（第 2 个义项：两条街交汇处）；句意是我在街角等人。

collocations.phrase: in the corner of the room
the four corners of the world

senses.title: The place where two lines or surfaces meet
senses.definition: the point or area where two edges, walls or surfaces meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条边、两面墙相交的点或区域
senses.example: The cat likes to sleep in the corner of the classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫喜欢睡在教室的角落里。
senses.why: Two walls closing in form a small hidden space, the picture of a corner.
senses.whyCN: 两面墙相夹形成隐蔽小空间，这正是角落的画面。

senses.title: The place where two streets meet
senses.definition: the area where two roads or streets join
senses.definitionCN: 两条道路交汇的地方
senses.example: There is a small bookshop at the street corner near our school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校附近的街角有家小书店。
senses.why: Streets meet just as walls do, so the city inherits the word.
senses.whyCN: 街道相交如墙角相接，城市沿用了这个词。

senses.title: To force someone into a difficult position
senses.definition: to trap someone so that they cannot escape
senses.definitionCN: 把某人困住使其无法脱身
senses.example: The question cornered him, and he had to tell the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题把他逼到了墙角，他只好说出实话。
senses.why: A person at the corner has walls on two sides and nowhere to run.
senses.whyCN: 被逼到角落的人两侧是墙，无处可逃。

senses.title: A difficult or remote position
senses.definition: a difficult situation or a distant small place
senses.definitionCN: 困难的处境或偏远的小地方
senses.example: The club helps students in far corners of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家社团帮助城市偏远角落的学生。
senses.why: Corners are far from the centre, so they stand for distant places or hard spots.
senses.whyCN: 角落远离中心，因此代指偏远之地或困难处境。

intro.en: Corner is not about corn at all, though it sounds like it.
intro.cn: corner 虽然听起来像 corn，却与谷物无关。

items.en: The Latin word cornu meant a horn, the hard point on an animal's head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cornu 意为角，即动物头上的坚硬尖角。

items.en: Old French turned cornu into corniere, the horn-shaped point.
items.cn: 古法语把 cornu 变成 corniere，指角状的尖点。

items.en: Norse hornna reinforced the horn idea in northern speech.
items.cn: 北欧语 hornna 在北方语言中强化了角的意象。

items.en: English blended these forms into corner in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语把多种形式融合成 corner。

items.en: Later corner spread from walls to streets, sports fields and even traps.
items.cn: 后来 corner 从墙角扩展到街角、球场，甚至引申为困境。

note.en: Some words share the horn root, others rhyme with corner.
note.cn: 有的词共享「角」词根，有的与 corner 押韵形似。

examples.en: Turn left at the next corner and you will see the library.

examples.cn: 期末考试近在眼前，现在就开始复习吧。

definition_en: right and without mistakes; to make something right
core_image: 老师用红笔把错字圈出来，写上正确答案
scene: 发数学卷子时，同桌发现自己把小数点点错了位置。The teacher corrected the mistake with her red pen.
sceneCN: 这里 correct 是动词「改正」（第 4 个义项：使变得正确）；句意是老师用红笔改正了错误。

derivatives.zh: 由 correct 加 -ion 构成，义为「改正；批改」
由 correct 加 -ly 构成，义为「正确地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不正确的」

senses.title: Right; without mistakes
senses.definition: right according to facts or rules
senses.definitionCN: 符合事实或规则
senses.example: Your spelling is all correct this time.
senses.exampleCN: 这次你的拼写全对。
senses.why: The root means made straight, and straight work has no bends or errors.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「扶正」，笔直的答卷没有弯折和错误。

senses.title: Proper; socially suitable
senses.definition: suitable for a situation or polite behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 适合场合或礼貌的行为
senses.example: Wearing a tie is correct for the speech contest.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲比赛打领带是得体的。
senses.why: A straight, upright posture is also what society calls proper.
senses.whyCN: 端正的姿态也是社会认可的得体。

senses.title: To point out and fix mistakes
senses.definition: to show someone their mistakes and make them right
senses.definitionCN: 指出错误并使之正确
senses.example: Our teacher corrects our essays every week.
senses.exampleCN: 老师每周批改我们的作文。
senses.why: Correcting straightens the crooked part of an answer.
senses.whyCN: 纠正是把答案中歪斜的部分扶直。

senses.title: To make something right
senses.definition: to change something so that it becomes right
senses.definitionCN: 通过改变使某事变得正确
senses.example: Please correct the wrong numbers in this report.
senses.exampleCN: 请改正报告里的错误数字。
senses.why: The verb keeps its Latin force: to set straight what bent.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留拉丁语的力度：把弯的东西扳直。

intro.en: Correct literally means made straight again.
intro.cn: correct 的字面意思是「重新扶正」。

items.en: The Latin verb corrigere meant to make straight, from com- (intensive) + regere (to make straight, rule).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 corrigere 意为扶正，由 com-（加强）+ regere（使直、统治）构成。

items.en: The past participle correctus described what had been set straight.
items.cn: 过去分词 correctus 描述已被扶正之物。

items.en: French carried correger and related forms into scholarship.
items.cn: 法语把 correger 等形式带入学术语。

items.en: English adopted correct in the fourteenth century for fixing texts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 correct，用于校订文本。

items.en: Today it covers school marks, manners and even politics.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖分数、礼仪乃至政治语境。

note.en: These words share the reg root of ruling straight, or mark rightness.
note.cn: 这些词共享 reg（使直、统治）词根，或表示正确。

normalIntro.en: Correct is the word made straight.

normal.en: correct sounds like kerect; an erect posture helps correct answers.
normal.cn: correct 音近「可睿克特」，睿智作答全对。

abstract.en: Picture a red tick beside every right answer.
abstract.cn: 想象每个正确答案旁的红勾。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked fence straightened post by post.
abstract.cn: 想象歪斜的篱笆被一根根扶正。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing a perfectly straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子画出笔直的线。

examples.en: Choose the correct word for each blank in the exercise.
examples.cn: 在练习中为每个空选出正确的单词。

examples.en: The teacher corrected my pronunciation of Thursday.
examples.cn: 老师纠正了我 Thursday 的发音。

examples.en: Reading the question twice helps you give correct answers.
examples.cn: 把题目读两遍有助于给出正确答案。

sensesIntro.cn: 从「扶正」引申为正确、得体与纠正。

core.cn: 核心意象：把歪的东西扳直

definition_en: in a right way, without mistakes
core_image: 指南针稳稳指向北，分毫不差
scene: 实验课上同学们轮流读出量筒的刻度。You must read the scale correctly in a science test.

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的原形，义为「正确的」

同根名词，义为「改正」

senses.title: In a right way without mistakes
senses.definition: in the way that is right, without errors
senses.definitionCN: 以正确的方式，没有错误
senses.example: She answered every maths question correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 她正确地答出了每道数学题。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the made-straight image: the action runs straight, with no crooked steps.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留扶正的意象：动作笔直进行，没有歪斜环节。

senses.title: In the standard or accepted way
senses.definition: according to the accepted rule or standard
senses.definitionCN: 按照公认的规则或标准
senses.example: Please hold the tennis racket correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 请按规范握好网球拍。
senses.why: What is straight by the rule is also what everyone accepts as proper.
senses.whyCN: 规则上笔直的也是大家认可得体的。

senses.title: Working as it should
senses.definition: working in the way it is designed to work
senses.definitionCN: 按设计的方式运行
senses.example: The new projector works correctly in every classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 新投影仪在每个教室都运行正常。
senses.why: A machine made straight runs straight, so correctly also describes devices.
senses.whyCN: 造得周正的机器运转顺畅，correctly 也形容设备。

intro.en: Correctly simply adds the adverb ending to correct.
intro.cn: correctly 只是给 correct 加上副词后缀。

items.en: The suffix -ly turned the adjective into an adverb.

items.en: correctly became common in schools and technical writing.
items.cn: correctly 在学校和科技文体中广泛使用。

items.en: Today it measures answers, manners and machines alike.
items.cn: 如今它衡量答案、礼仪和机器。

note.en: These adverbs measure rightness or its failures.

normal.en: -ly turns adjectives into adverbs.

abstract.cn: 想象箭笔直飞向靶心。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tapping the exact right key.
abstract.cn: 想象手指按准正确的键。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist with every box ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象清单上每个格子都打了勾。

examples.en: You must copy the address correctly into the form.

examples.en: The team worked correctly and finished the experiment first.

examples.en: If the clock is set correctly, it never runs slow.

definition_en: the money needed to buy or do something; to have a price
core_image: 收银台跳出的数字，付出去就不回来了
scene: 春游前大家讨论要不要租自行车环湖。The bike hire will cost each of us twenty yuan.
sceneCN: 这里 cost 是动词「花费」（第 1 个义项：需要付出钱）；句意是租车每人要花二十元。

derivatives.zh: 由 cost 加 -ly 构成，义为「昂贵的」
义为「成本核算」

senses.title: To have a price
senses.definition: to have a particular price
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个价格
senses.example: This dictionary costs fifty yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 这本词典五十元。
senses.why: Cost is the constant: the price stands at what it stands.
senses.whyCN: cost 是恒定值：价格就停在那里。

senses.title: To make someone lose something valuable
senses.definition: to make someone lose money, time or something important
senses.definitionCN: 使某人失去钱、时间或重要之物
senses.example: The wrong turn cost us an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走错路让我们损失了一个小时。
senses.why: Money is only one thing the price can take; time and chances can also be paid.
senses.whyCN: 钱只是代价的一种；时间和机会同样可能被付出。

senses.title: The money needed for something
senses.definition: the amount of money needed to buy or do something
senses.definitionCN: 购买或做某事所需的钱数
senses.example: The total cost of the school trip is three hundred yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 学校春游的总费用是三百元。
senses.why: The noun names the number itself, the price tag.
senses.whyCN: 名词指那个数字本身，即价格标签。

senses.title: What must be given up
senses.definition: something lost or given up to gain another thing
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而失去或付出的东西
senses.example: He saved the drowning child at the cost of his own phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他救起溺水孩子时牺牲了自己的手机。
senses.why: Every gain has a shadow price, the cost behind the win.
senses.whyCN: 每次获得都有影子价格，即胜利背后的代价。

intro.en: Cost began as a Latin word for standing together, then stood for a price.

items.en: The Latin verb constare meant to stand firm or to be fixed at, from com- (together) + stare (to stand).

definition_en: clothes worn for a play, a party or to look like someone
core_image: 万圣节南瓜斗篷一披，普通同学瞬间变成小巫师
scene: 学校艺术节要演小红帽，大家为戏服忙了一下午。Her wolf costume made everyone laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 costume 是「戏服」（第 1 个义项：演出穿的服装）；句意是她的狼戏服把大家逗乐了。

derivatives.zh: 由 costume 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着戏服的」
同根词 custom，义为「习俗」，是 costume 的词源核心

senses.title: Special clothes for a performance or party
senses.definition: clothes worn to look like a character in a play or at a party
senses.definitionCN: 为扮演角色或在聚会时穿的衣服
senses.example: The actors changed into their animal costumes backstage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们在后台换上了动物戏服。
senses.why: Custom means habit, and stage clothes follow the custom of the character.
senses.whyCN: custom 意为习俗，戏服遵循角色的习俗。

senses.title: The traditional dress of a place or time
senses.definition: the typical clothes of a country, group or period
senses.definitionCN: 某国、某群体或某时代的典型服装
senses.example: She wore a beautiful national costume at the culture festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她在文化节上穿了漂亮的民族服装。
senses.why: Costume also means the dress a custom hands down through years.
senses.whyCN: costume 也指习俗流传多年的服饰。

senses.title: A set of clothes worn together
senses.definition: clothes of one style worn as a set
senses.definitionCN: 风格统一的一套衣服
senses.example: His swimming costume was left at home by mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他的泳衣被忘在了家里。
senses.why: The pieces belong together like one character's outfit.
senses.whyCN: 各件属于一套，如同一个角色的行头。

intro.en: Costume grew from the same root as custom, habits of dressing.
intro.cn: costume 与 custom 同根，都是穿着的习俗。

items.en: The Latin word consuetudo meant custom or habit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 意为习俗、习惯。

items.en: Italian costume meant custom, and then the customary style of dress.
items.cn: 意大利语 costume 意为习俗，进而指惯常的衣着风格。

items.en: French costume carried both custom and dress into learned writing.
items.cn: 法语 costume 兼指习俗与服饰，进入书面语。

items.en: English adopted costume in the eighteenth century for period dress.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪吸收 costume，指某时代的服装。

items.en: Theatre and parties made costume mean dress-up clothes today.
items.cn: 如今剧场与聚会让 costume 指化装服饰。

note.en: These words share the custom root or name clothes.
note.cn: 这些词共享 custom 词根或表示服装。

examples.cn: 我们为学校话剧做了恐龙戏服。

examples.en: Each region in China has its own traditional costume.
examples.cn: 中国各地都有自己的传统服饰。

examples.en: Remember to bring your swimming costume for the pool trip.

definition_en: a soft white fibre used to make cloth and thread
core_image: 云朵一样的白色棉桃，从田里走进T恤衫
scene: 体育课前，老师提醒大家换上吸汗的纯棉运动衫再上跑道。In PE class the teacher asked us to wear pure cotton shirts for the running practice.
sceneCN: 这里 cotton 是「棉布」（第 2 个义项：棉纤维织的布）；句意是跑步练习要穿棉质T恤。

derivatives.zh: cotton 与 wood 合成，义为「棉白杨」
由 cotton 加 -y 构成，义为「似棉花的」

senses.title: The soft white fibre of the cotton plant
senses.definition: the soft white wool-like fibre around cotton seeds
senses.definitionCN: 棉籽周围棉絮状的白色软纤维
senses.example: Farmers pick cotton in the fields every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天农民在田里摘棉花。
senses.why: The plant makes soft white balls, like little clouds on the field.
senses.whyCN: 植株结出白色软球，像田里的小云朵。

senses.title: Cloth or thread made from the fibre
senses.definition: thread or cloth woven from cotton fibre
senses.definitionCN: 用棉纤维纺成或织成的线与布
senses.example: These cotton curtains feel soft and breathe well.
senses.exampleCN: 这些棉窗帘手感柔软又透气。
senses.why: The fibre is spun and woven, so the word covers the cloth too.
senses.whyCN: 纤维被纺织成布，词义随之覆盖布料。

senses.title: The cotton plant itself
senses.definition: the plant that produces the fibre
senses.definitionCN: 生产这种纤维的植物
senses.example: Bees buzzed over the cotton growing near the village.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂在村子附近的棉田上方嗡嗡飞。
senses.why: From fibre the name goes back to the living plant.
senses.whyCN: 词义从纤维回溯到活体植株。

intro.en: Cotton travelled into English from Arabic along trade routes.
intro.cn: cotton 沿着商路从阿拉伯语走进英语。

items.en: Arabic qutn or qutun named the cotton plant.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 qutn 指棉花植株。

items.en: Spanish algodon, from Arabic with the article al-, carried the word west.
items.cn: 西班牙语 algodon 带着阿拉伯语冠词 al- 把词传向西边。

items.en: Old French coton spread it further north.
items.cn: 古法语 coton 把词传向更北。

items.en: English adopted cotton in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 cotton。

items.en: The industrial revolution made cotton the cloth of the world.
items.cn: 工业革命使棉布走向世界。

note.en: These words name fibres and cloths like cotton.
note.cn: 这些词指像棉花一样的纤维与布料。

definition_en: to push air out of your throat suddenly with a rough sound
core_image: 喉咙里发痒，一口气猛地冲出来，咳咳两声
scene: 秋游吹了冷风，小明一路轻咳。He kept coughing on the windy bus home.
sceneCN: 这里 cough 是「咳嗽」（第 1 个义项：喉咙突然排气）；句意是回程车上风大，他一直咳嗽。

derivatives.zh: cough 与 drop 合成，义为「止咳糖」
义为「咳嗽（动作）」

senses.title: To push air out of the throat suddenly
senses.definition: to force air out of the lungs with a sudden loud sound
senses.definitionCN: 以突发的响声把空气从肺部排出
senses.example: Cover your mouth when you cough in class.
senses.exampleCN: 在教室咳嗽时要捂住嘴。
senses.why: The throat clears itself with a burst of air, the body's quick sweep.
senses.whyCN: 喉咙以一股急气自我清扫，这是身体的快速打扫。

senses.title: To force something out of the throat
senses.definition: to bring something up from the throat or chest by coughing
senses.definitionCN: 通过咳嗽把东西从喉咙或胸口排出
senses.example: He coughed up the fish bone safely.
senses.exampleCN: 他安全地咳出了鱼刺。
senses.why: The burst of air can carry small trouble out of the chest.
senses.whyCN: 这股急气能把胸腔里的小麻烦带出来。

senses.title: An illness marked by coughing
senses.definition: an illness that makes you cough often
senses.definitionCN: 让人不断咳嗽的疾病
senses.example: A bad cough kept her home for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 严重的咳嗽让她在家休息了两天。
senses.why: The action names the sickness that repeats it.
senses.whyCN: 动作之名转指反复出现的病症。

examples.cn: 运动后咳嗽就喝点温水。

definition_zh: can 的过去式；能够；可以；可能
definition_en: past form of can; used to ask politely or show possibility
core_image: 一只悬而未落的手，可能性停在半空
scene: 哥哥问我要不要一起去图书馆，我正想做手工。Could you pass me the glue stick, please?
sceneCN: 这里 could 是「能否；可以」（第 3 个义项：礼貌请求）；句意是请帮我递一下胶棒好吗？

pos.zh: 能够；可以（can 的过去式）；可能

derivatives.zh: could 的现在式，义为「能；可以」
could not 的缩略，义为「不能」

senses.title: Past ability
senses.definition: the past form of can, showing past ability
senses.definitionCN: can 的过去式，表示过去的能力
senses.example: When he was five, he could swim across the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他五岁时就能游过泳池。
senses.why: The word remembers what once stood within reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个词记得那些曾经触手可及的能力。

senses.title: Possibility
senses.definition: used to say something is possible
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能
senses.example: It could rain before the sports meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 运动会开始前可能会下雨。
senses.why: What was once able to happen is still able to happen, so could also means maybe.
senses.whyCN: 曾经可能发生的现在仍可能发生，所以 could 也表示「也许」。

senses.title: A polite request or offer
senses.definition: used to ask for something politely
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请求或提供帮助
senses.example: Could I borrow your eraser for a minute?
senses.exampleCN: 我能借你的橡皮用一下吗？
senses.why: Distancing the request in past form softens it, a gentle politeness trick.
senses.whyCN: 用过去式拉开请求的距离，是委婉的礼貌技巧。

senses.title: An unreal or imagined situation
senses.definition: used for imaginary or unlikely situations
senses.definitionCN: 用于想象或不太可能的情况
senses.example: If I could fly, I would visit my grandma every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 如果我能飞，我每个周末都去看奶奶。
senses.why: Could keeps the action in imagination, never in fact.
senses.whyCN: could 把动作留在想象中，而非事实里。

intro.en: Could grew from can, with an old -l- ending that no longer means much.
intro.cn: could 由 can 加古老的 -l- 词尾演变而来。

items.en: The verb cunnan meant to know how; its past was cuðe.
items.cn: 古英语动词 cunnan 意为知晓、会，过去式为 cuðe。

items.en: A rare double past ending -de fused into coude.
items.cn: 中世纪英语中罕见的双重过去式词尾 -de 融合成 coude。

items.en: Northern and Scottish spelling added an l by analogy with would and should.
items.cn: 北方与苏格兰拼法类比 would 和 should 加上了 l。

items.en: The l spread to standard English though it was never pronounced.
items.cn: 这个 l 虽从不发音，却扩散到标准英语。

items.en: Could now covers ability, chance and polite requests.
items.cn: 如今 could 涵盖能力、可能性与礼貌请求。

note.en: These modals walk together and confuse writers.
note.cn: 这些情态动词结伴而行，也常令人混淆。

entries.definition: past form of will; polite forms
entries.definitionCN: 将会；愿意（will 的过去式）

normalIntro.en: Could is can wearing a soft hat.
normalIntro.cn: could 是戴了软帽子的 can。

normal.en: could is the past of can.
normal.cn: could 是 can 的过去式。

normal.en: could you please makes requests polite.
normal.cn: could you please 让请求更礼貌。

normal.en: could have done means a missed chance.
normal.cn: could have done 指本可做到却没做。

normal.en: could be means maybe.
normal.cn: could be 意为可能是。

normal.en: could sounds like kood; a kind mood could help you a lot.
normal.cn: could 音近「苦的」，去不成的遗憾带点苦味。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open by a polite hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只礼貌的手扶住门。

abstract.en: Picture grey clouds that could rain but might not.
abstract.cn: 想象可能下雨也可能不下阴云。

abstract.en: Picture an old photo of a five-year-old swimmer.
abstract.cn: 想象五岁游泳老照片。

examples.en: Could you help me carry these books to the library?
examples.cn: 你能帮我把这些书搬到图书馆吗？

examples.en: Last year I couldn't skate, but now I can.
examples.cn: 去年我还不会滑冰，现在会了。

examples.en: That noise could be the wind in the trees.
examples.cn: 那声音可能是风穿过树梢。

definition_zh: 数；计算；把……算入；数数；总数
definition_en: to say numbers in order; to include; the total found by counting
core_image: 指尖点着跳绳的次数，一二三四五
scene: 体育课测跳绳，同桌帮小芳记数。She managed one hundred and two skips, counting every one.
sceneCN: 这里 count 是动词「数」（第 1 个义项：按顺序报数）；句意是她跳了一百零二下，每一下都数了。

derivatives.zh: 由 count 加 -er 构成，义为「计数器；柜台」
由 count 加 -able 构成，义为「可数的」

senses.title: To say numbers in order
senses.definition: to say numbers one by one to find a total
senses.definitionCN: 逐一报数以求总数
senses.example: Let's count how many players are on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 我们数数场上有多少球员。
senses.why: The root means to reckon, moving item by item like steps.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是计算，像迈步一样逐项清点。

senses.title: To include or matter
senses.definition: to include someone or something; to be important
senses.definitionCN: 把某人某物计入；起重要作用
senses.example: Every point counts in the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛中每一分都很关键。
senses.why: What is counted is taken into the total, so counted things matter.
senses.whyCN: 被计入的进入总数，所以被计数之物重要。

senses.title: The act or total of counting
senses.definition: the action of finding a number, or the number found
senses.definitionCN: 计数的行为或所得的数字
senses.example: The count of the class vote was twenty-eight.
senses.exampleCN: 班级投票的计票结果是二十八票。
senses.why: The verb's work becomes a noun number.
senses.whyCN: 动词的成果化为名词数字。

senses.title: To rely on someone
senses.definition: to depend on or trust someone to help
senses.definitionCN: 信任并依赖某人
senses.example: You can count on me to bring the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 放心，球我来带。
senses.why: Counting someone in means their help is in your total.
senses.whyCN: 把某人算进来意味着其助力计入你的总数。

intro.en: Count came from Latin through French, from a word for reckoning.
intro.cn: count 经法语源自拉丁语的「计算」一词。

items.en: The Latin verb computare meant to reckon or calculate, from com- (together) + putare (to think, reckon).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 computare 意为计算，由 com-（共同）+ putare（思考、估算）构成。

items.en: Old French counter meant to count or reckon.
items.cn: 古法语 counter 意为数、计算。

items.en: English adopted count in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 count。

items.en: The same French word named a noble, the count, keeper of accounts.
items.cn: 同一法语词还指掌管账目的贵族伯爵。

items.en: Modern uses spread to votes, ranks and even rhythm in music.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到计票、级别甚至音乐节拍。

note.en: These words share the reckon root or name counting.
note.cn: 这些词共享「计算」词根或与计数相关。

normalIntro.en: Count is the thinking root put to numbers.
normalIntro.cn: count 是把思考词根用于数字。

normal.en: count = com- (together) + putare (reckon).
normal.cn: count 由 com-（共同）+ putare（计算）构成。

normal.en: account and counter share the root.
normal.cn: account 和 counter 同根。

normal.en: count on means rely on.
normal.cn: count on 意为依靠。

normal.en: every second counts means every moment matters.
normal.cn: every second counts 指每分每秒都重要。

normal.en: count sounds like kaont; count your coins one by one.
normal.cn: count 音近「靠他」，数数的时候靠他帮忙记。

abstract.cn: 想象手指随跳绳一下下点击。

abstract.en: Picture votes stacked in a clear column.
abstract.cn: 想象选票排成清晰的一列。

abstract.en: Picture a friend arriving exactly when promised.

examples.en: We counted thirty-two students on the playground.
examples.cn: 我们数出操场上有三十二名学生。

examples.en: You can count on our team in the relay race.
examples.cn: 接力赛你可以指望我们队。

examples.cn: 裁判用卡片记录得分。
